question:
A professional road cyclist is considering whether to inject synthetic erythropoietin (EPO) rather than relying solely on altitude training to improve performance.
Evaluate the choice to inject EPO instead of relying on altitude training alone. Refer to the physiological effects of EPO on the cyclist in your answer.
markScheme:
AO1 - Altitude training carried out at 2500m+ above sea level, where lower pO2 leads to increased EPO. EPO is a naturally occurring hormone; synthetic EPO can be manufactured. EPO increases red blood cell count/haemoglobin/O2 carrying capacity/delays OBLA.
AO2 - EPO/altitude training increases the cyclist's ability to work aerobically at high intensity, maintaining speed throughout a race, allows sprinting at the finish, and faster recovery.
AO3 - Why inject: EPO can be injected quickly with no interruption to training; avoids the acclimatisation/sickness of altitude training; benefits sustained for longer avoiding peaking difficulties; avoids time away from home.
Why not inject: EPO is banned - risk of being banned from the sport/loss of income/damaged reputation; unfair advantage, immoral/against fair play; increased risk of blood clots/stroke.
Accept any other appropriate evaluation.
Max 8 marks.

question:
A significant number of athletes have had drug test samples retrospectively found to be positive following re-analysis using improved testing methods some years after a major Games.
Evaluate the effectiveness of strategies used for eliminating the use of performance enhancing drugs in sport.
markScheme:
AO1 - Educate athletes/coaches of the risks of PEDs; use high-profile drug-free role models; invest in drug screening/detection research; co-ordinate nations' testing regulations; more frequent randomised testing; stricter punishments.
AO2 - National education programmes for young athletes; role models advocating clean sport; accredited laboratories worldwide; whereabouts systems; standardised testing protocols across countries; biological passports; lifetime bans/repayment of earnings acting as financial deterrents.
AO3 - Effective: co-operation leads to more consistent regulations/protocols/punishments; shared costs of testing; samples retained and retested for years after events; whereabouts systems mean athletes cannot avoid testing; harsh punishments deter athletes.
Ineffective: testing athletes training abroad is difficult; masking agents constantly evolve; not all countries follow the same guidelines; loopholes such as therapeutic use exemptions are exploited; the rewards of success may outweigh the risk for some.
Accept other appropriate evaluation.
Max 15 marks.

question:
Following allegations of a state-sponsored doping programme, athletes representing one nation were excluded from competing at a recent major international multi-sport event.
Analyse the social, physiological and psychological reasons for an athlete to take drugs and the short-term and long-term implications this could have.
markScheme:
AO1 - Social reasons: win-at-all-costs ethos, fame and fortune, pressure to win, belief testers can be evaded, state-sponsored programmes. Psychological reasons vary by drug, eg beta blockers to steady nerves, anabolic steroids to increase aggression, stimulants to raise confidence. Physiological reasons: anabolic steroids aid protein storage and muscle hypertrophy; beta blockers reduce heart rate improving accuracy; EPO increases red blood cell production improving aerobic capacity.
AO2 - Potential medallists may dope for sponsorship/media profile; state-sponsored athletes required to follow instructions; golfers/snooker players may use beta blockers for accuracy; combat athletes may use steroids to increase aggression; weightlifters may use steroids for strength/power; endurance cyclists may use EPO for aerobic capacity.
AO3 - Damaged reputation/lost sponsorship if caught; long-term financial struggle; steroids can cause mood swings/paranoia affecting training and relationships; increased aggression can lead to rule-breaking and bans; EPO can cause blood clots/strokes; steroids can cause kidney failure; whole nations' athletes may be treated with suspicion and face stricter testing.
The specification only requires knowledge of EPO, anabolic steroids and beta blockers, but other correct and relevant PEDs should be credited.
Accept any other appropriate analysis.
Max 15 marks.

question: Explain the possible advantages of taking beta blockers and identify the type of sporting activities in which they may be used.
markScheme:
Beta blockers block the effects of adrenaline/slow the sympathetic nervous system/slow heart rate/lower blood pressure, used for activities requiring accuracy, eg archery, snooker, shooting or equivalent.
Need advantage and sporting activity.
Max 2 marks.

question:
Some athletes choose to take illegal performance enhancing drugs, such as erythropoietin (EPO), beta blockers or anabolic steroids.
Evaluate why a sprinter and a marathon runner may choose to take performance enhancing drugs for physiological benefit.
markScheme:
AO1 - EPO naturally produced in the kidney but can be artificially manufactured to increase red blood cell count/haemoglobin. Beta blockers block the effects of adrenaline/slow heart rate. Anabolic steroids are synthetic hormones resembling testosterone that promote muscle growth.
AO2 - Sprinters more likely to use anabolic steroids to increase strength/power and remain lean; unlikely to use beta blockers or EPO as these do not match a sprinter's needs. Marathon runners unlikely to use steroids or beta blockers, more likely to use EPO as the event uses the aerobic system and requires oxygen delivery rather than anaerobic power.
AO3 - Sprinters using steroids increase anaerobic power needed out of the blocks and to maintain speed; aids protein storage/muscle growth; leaner body weight improves sprint performance. Marathon runners need more oxygen carried around the body over a long race; more red blood cells reduce muscular fatigue, giving an advantage over rivals. Beta blockers reduce adrenaline effects; sprinters may use them to avoid a false start but the benefit is smaller than steroids; not useful for marathon runners who do not rely on fine motor precision.
Accept any other evaluative point relating to the physiological benefits to a sprinter and/or marathon runner.
Max 15 marks.

question: Evaluate the reasons why elite athletes will resort to taking illegal performance enhancing drugs.
markScheme:
- Winning margins are normally slender in power events, so a PED that gives bigger/stronger muscles could mean the difference between winning and losing (1)
- Long distance events rely on high levels of endurance, so some feel that without PEDs they cannot sustain energy production for the duration of the race (1)
- Elite competition creates high pressure situations which may negatively impact performance; taking PEDs to reduce anxiety/steady nerves gives a greater chance of performing at their optimum (1)
Accept other relevant evaluation points.
Max 3 marks.

question: Explain the problems faced by sporting organisations when implementing a ban on the use of performance enhancing drugs.
markScheme:
5 marks for 5 of:
- Difficulty in accurate testing/masking agents/new drugs/difficult to keep testing up to date/cheats always one step ahead of testers
- Some drugs used for medical reasons/difficulty in classifying drugs
- Athletes motivated to take drugs as high rewards available/lack of support from sponsors when athletes are banned
- Illegal support provided by some NGBs/coaches/countries/fellow competitors
- Inconsistent policies for testing or punishments/countries and governing bodies have different policies
- Cost of testing expensive/time consuming
- Legal challenge to positive results
- Difficulty gaining access to athletes for testing/out-of-season testing difficult
- Difficulty in issuing an appropriate ban/clean athletes may be caught up in blanket bans
Max 5 marks.

question:
Performance enhancing substances have been used in sport since ancient times.
Suggest reasons to support the argument for legalising drugs in sport today.
markScheme:
4 marks for 4 of:
- Drugs can be masked/occur naturally in the body/EPO/gene doping/found in common medication
- Drugs so easily available/impossible to eliminate use of drugs
- Overall low rate of testing/inaccurate results/cheats one step ahead of testers
- Negative impact of poor testing affects performers' reputation/careers/sponsorship deals or equivalent
- Drugs, if regulated, are not so harmful/labs could be encouraged to produce safe performance enhancers
- If everyone could take them it would become a level playing field
- Limited resources could be better employed, eg to detect harmful drugs/develop elite sport in other ways
- Drugs are necessary to recover from gruelling training
- Other technological advantages aren't regulated against, eg biomechanics/nutrition/oxygen tents
- Sports and countries have different rules
- Individuals have the right to choose/it's their body
- Spectators/supporters not disappointed by role models
Max 4 marks.

question:

- Encourages drug taking from an early age/perception 'if you don't take it, you won't make it'/peer pressure

question:
Sporting organisations work together to develop elite performers and to ensure that they understand doping regulations.
Explain the advantages and the disadvantages of all sports, in all countries, testing for performance enhancing drugs.
markScheme:
4 marks for 4 of (sub max of 2 marks)
Advantages: uphold traditions/sporting ethics/cheats caught/all competitors equal/no country or performer has an advantage.
Standard list of banned substances/same testing procedures/similar punishments.
Random tests more effective/testing not limited by where an athlete is based.
Shared costs between all sports.
Performers not able to 'pick and choose' sports based on testing procedures/no basis for legal complaints of unfair treatment.
Disadvantages: difficult to get all countries/sports to agree.
Expensive/limited number of testing facilities/not available in all countries.
Testing can produce incorrect/inconsistent results/difficult to keep up with new drugs.
Difficult to agree which PEDs should be included in banned lists.
Professionals have the right to decide on their own development needs.
Money used for testing could be used for education about the dangers of drug taking.
Max 4 marks.
